title: Apoptosis or necrosis?
caption: Apoptosis is a controlled, energy-requiring suicide: the cell shrinks and breaks into apoptotic bodies that phagocytes remove quietly. Necrosis follows severe injury: the cell swells and bursts, and its contents leak out and cause inflammation.
alt: A flow chart: a controlled, energy-requiring death triggered by signals leads to apoptosis, with shrinking and no inflammation; death from severe injury leads to necrosis, with swelling, bursting and inflammation.
description: Is the death controlled and energy-requiring, triggered by a signal such as DNA damage or a death receptor? If so it is apoptosis: the cell shrinks, the DNA is cut up, apoptotic bodies form and phagocytes remove them without inflammation.
If the cause is severe injury (lack of oxygen, toxins, trauma) it is necrosis: the cell swells and its membrane ruptures, and its contents leak out and cause inflammation.
